IncidentBot: INC-32200 created (sev=P1) - embeddings-prod (us-west-2) abnormal fanout and rising 5xxs. Paging SREs.
Maria: paging SRE + sec. Alerts: embeddings.queue-length x4, edge-5xx spike, KV misses up. Seen from POST /v1/embeddings/batch primarily.
Sam: ack, looking. Edge CPU high, many concurrent connections from rotating client IPs. Pulling request headers now.
Leo: security looking. Patterns: repeated batch jobs with similar bearer token prefixes, user-agent variations that match known scraping frameworks. ASN clustering across two proxy providers.
Maria: likely abusive fanout. Proposals: 1) short-term WAF block on offending ASNs 2) per-key emergency token bucket (reduce bursts) 3) disable batch uploads (stop amplification) 4) enable low-trust challenge for anonymous keys 5) status update. Who owns?
Sam: I'm on WAF + quota. Avani you take comms? Leo you confirm challenge feasibility.
Sam: running: `wafctl add-block-asn --ids 7018,36351 --reason "embed-fanout-32200"` -> created rules wb-32200-a, wb-32200-b.
InfraBot: feature-flag toggle applied: ff.disable_batch_embeddings=true by Sam at 3220019950.
Sam: pushing quota change: `quotactl apply --policy emergency-emb-32200 --per_key_rate 30/min` -> qp-32200. Applied to non-enterprise keys.
Sam: initial effect: queue length falling, 5xxs down ~60%, single-shot embeddings latency small bump.
Leo: enabling anon challenge flow (captcha) for unknown keys: `authctl set-challenge anon=true` -> ff.anon_challenge=on. Early telemetry shows 70% reduction from low-trust tokens.
Avani: drafting status: "We're actively mitigating an embeddings traffic surge that is causing transient errors. We've applied temporary traffic controls and may disable batch uploads for non-enterprise keys. We'll follow up with timeline and remediation." Posting once Sam confirms stability.
Jake: CS reports from two small customers seeing bulk import failures; they've been informed and request ETA for batch re-enable.
Maria: add fallback model routing for non-critical traffic to reduce pressure: route->model-emb-small (lower compute). Sam can you add rate-limit 429 after sustained bursts for offending keys?
Sam: added fallback route fr-32200 to model-emb-small for low-priority keys. Edge policy: token-burst 5 -> 429. Rule id fr-32200. Monitoring dashboards updated.
Sam: also added short lived CDN-level IP blocklist for top 500 offenders to limit connection churn. Command: `cdnctl ban --list offenders_top500_32200`.
Leo: recommend creating a fingerprint-based block for the rotating botnet (UA+header combo) to avoid collateral ASN blocks. Will produce sig sig-32200-fprint.
Sam: added fingerprint rule sig-32200-fprint to WAF. Early counters show blocked matches increasing.
InfraBot: deploy log: edge-proxy config hot-reload completed at 3220020100.
Sam: metrics now: embeddings.5xx down 72%, queue length ~baseline +10%, edge CPU trending down. WAF blocked ~2.4M requests in last 10m.
Avani: status posted to status.redwood.ai and customer messages queued. Sending targeted note to enterprise contacts with next update in 1h.
Maria: prepping handoff in 20m. Nora will take overnight monitoring. Sam please attach runbook snippet and rule IDs here before handoff.
Sam: runbook items: WAF: wb-32200-a, wb-32200-b, sig-32200-fprint; Quota policy qp-32200; FFs: disable_batch_embeddings=true, anon_challenge=true; Fallback route fr-32200; CDN ban list offenders_top500_32200. Primary watch metrics: embeddings.5xx, embed_queue.length, edge_tcp_conns, kv_cache.miss_rate.
Nora: ack - taking on monitoring at 3220021300. Will escalate to oncall if 5xx rises >10% over baseline or if new ASN clusters appear. Thanks team :thumbsup:.
IncidentBot: INC-32200 status -> mitigated -> responders continue monitoring. Close paging when stable for 45m.
